newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania's central bank cuts key interest rates.
newsitem.headline: Romania's central bank cuts key interest rates.

text.p: Romania's (central) National Bank (BNR) said on Monday it had cut the discount rate -- its key indicative rate -- to 40 from 50 percent, easing monetary policy after a slowdown in monthly inflation.
The bank's board also decided to slash the Lombard rate to an annual 140 percent from 200 percent, BNR communication manager Adrian Vasilescu told Reuters.
He said the changes in the rates became effective July 15.
Monthly inflation dropped to 2.3 percent last month from 4.3 percent in May and compared with a record high of 30.7 percent in March when fuel, energy and food prices were liberalised.

Earlier this year the BNR raised the discount and Lombard rates, tightening monetary policy to fight inflation and meet International Monetary Fund recommendations that the discount rate should be positive in real terms.

The discount rate has been stable at 50 percent since January. The Lombard rate, charged for overdraft credits, was fixed at 200 percent three months ago after touching a record high of 682.4 percent late in February.
BNR governor Mugur Isarescu said in May the bank would like to engineer a careful reduction in interest rates to allow the economy to recover after tough monetary policies.
